title: Business law issues — Westgate Supply
instructions: Select the best answer for each situation involving Westgate Supply, Inc.

exhibits.title: Situations
exhibits.content:
1. Westgate orally agreed to buy $3,000 of shelving; the seller later denied the deal. Nothing was signed.
2. Westgate's purchasing manager (actual authority up to $10,000, which suppliers don't know about) signed a $15,000 order with a regular supplier.
3. A lender perfected a security interest in Westgate's equipment by filing on May 1. A second lender, who lent first on April 20, filed on May 10.
4. A seller delivered new equipment to Westgate on June 1 with a purchase-money security interest and filed on June 12.
5. Thirty days before filing a Chapter 7 petition while insolvent, Westgate repaid a $20,000 overdue loan to its president.
6. Westgate plans to sell $6 million of stock to 50 investors in a 12-month period, without advertising.

rows.label: 1. Oral shelving contract
options: Unenforceable under the statute of frauds unless an exception applies
rows.answer: Unenforceable under the statute of frauds unless an exception applies
rows.explanation: Goods of $500 or more require a signed writing.

rows.label: 2. The $15,000 order
options: Binding on Westgate through apparent authority
Void because it exceeds actual authority
rows.answer: Binding on Westgate through apparent authority
rows.explanation: Secret limits don't bind third parties who reasonably rely.

rows.label: 4. The equipment seller's PMSI
options: Has priority over both lenders in the new equipment
rows.answer: Has priority over both lenders in the new equipment
rows.explanation: A PMSI in equipment perfected within 20 days of delivery.

rows.label: 5. The repayment to the president
options: Recoverable by the trustee as a preferential transfer
Protected because it was within 90 days
rows.answer: Recoverable by the trustee as a preferential transfer
rows.explanation: An insider payment within 1 year while insolvent for an antecedent debt.

rows.label: 6. The stock offering
options: Must be registered with the SEC
rows.explanation: Rule 504 covers up to $10 million in 12 months.
